--- page 3 ---
Narrative text (Overview/Summary/Executive summary). Key figures: CERF allocated $7.5 million for typhoon season 2023; 2-stage trigger — (1) Readiness trigger 4-7 days prior to forecast landfall (TC potential category ≥3, >178 km/h 1-min sustained or 158 km/h 10-min sustained wind, projected to hit Region 5, 8, 13/Caraga); (2) Activation trigger on/before 72 hrs (3 days) prior to landfall using 510 model impact map, updated every 6-12 hrs. Scenario 1 covers Region 5 + Samar Island provinces (Region 8); Scenario 2 covers Region 13 (Caraga) + Leyte Island provinces (Region 8). Reach ~378,400 people (Scenario 1) and ~179,350 people (Scenario 2).

--- page 4 ---
Narrative text continuing Executive Summary — activation threshold detail: CERF AA activated if 72 hrs before landfall, predicted damaged houses fall between 50% probability of ≥80,000 houses totally damaged and 95% probability of ≥5,000 houses totally damaged. Describes "the Delivery": ~65% (Scenario 1) / 64% (Scenario 2) of budget as cash — blanket multi-purpose cash of US$62 (PhP 3,250, ~1/3 MEB) for 10 days to 75,600 households/378,000 beneficiaries (Scenario 1) and 35,800 households/179,000 beneficiaries (Scenario 2) via FAO, IOM, UNICEF, UNFPA, WFP. Details agency roles: FAO livelihood storage/cash for 400 HH & 15,500 agri-families, 77,900 agri-HH advisories; IOM modular tents + CBI shelter repair; UNFPA SRHR/GBV + cash for pregnant/vulnerable women; UNICEF cash top-up to 4Ps beneficiaries.

Narrative: Operational coordination with local authorities (NDRRMC/OCD, AA TWG co-chaired FAO+OCD). Mandatory pre-emptive evacuation procedure — since Typhoon Haiyan (6,000+ casualties), evacuations start 48h before landfall, complete 24h before; COVID-19 pushed prep to 72h before landfall; Nov 2020 saw 500,000 evacuated pre-Goni and 230,000 pre-Vamco. Consultation with communities: 2022 pre-crisis survey, 434 respondents across 20 municipalities (Region 5) + 24 municipalities (Region 8), 41-question tool across 5 sections.

--- page 25 ---
Narrative: Ensuring readiness for timely implementation — only ~48h between Readiness and Activation triggers; operational challenges (banking hours, telecom/power cutoffs, port closures at Wind Signal 1 ~72h ahead); staff duty-of-care equipment needs; simulation exercises July 2021 (1-day) and 19-23 Sept 2022 (2-day, both scenarios) testing risk communications, information flow, coordination, prepositioning, PSEA/AAP. Pre-emptive cash interventions: MPC value changed methodology to Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB, PHP 9,750/month, endorsed by HCT July 2023); AA MPC = PhP 3,250 (US$58) = 1/3 of MEB for 10-day lead period; budgeted as US$62 (7% FX buffer). 75,600 HH (Scenario 1) and 35,800 HH (Scenario 2) to receive MPC. Two-staged cash distribution: WFP/UNFPA/FAO trigger at 72h before landfall; IOM distributes near evacuation centres (72-48h ahead).

Table: cash-based interventions by agency — FAO: FSP modality, multi-purpose cash to 15,500 farmers/fisherfolk + 2,000 registered RSBSA, amount 977K*/124K**; IOM: Palawan/Direct Cash Pay-out, CBI shelter repair kits + MPCA to 12,785 families each scenario, 1.8M*/1.8M**; WFP: Western Union/Palawan/Direct Cash Payout, MPCA to 25,000 families (S1)/20,000 families (S2), 1.6M*/1.2M**; UNICEF: DSWD/Landbank, unconditional cash to 21,000 households (4Ps subset), 483K*; UNFPA: direct cash payout via local partners, MPC to 1,000 pregnant + 1,100 vulnerable women, 84K*/65K*. WFP interventions — objective to protect assets/lives/livelihoods via blanket MPC.

--- page 31 ---
Table continuation: WFP (TBD, FSAC) 2,172,107(S1)/1,890,890(S2) reaching 25,000 HH (S1)/20,000 HH (S2) — Multi-purpose unconditional cash-based transfer, plus COVID19 IPC supplies/WASH materials. Section 5 Pre-agreed Financing / CERF: ERC agreed to allocate up to $140 million from CERF (Rapid Response window, no separate "AA window") for AA pilots globally; disburses on no-regrets basis once (1) RC/HC endorsement, (2) ERC pre-approval, (3) trigger activated within 2 years of pre-approval. Philippines pilot: $7.5M (2021/2022, extended to end 2024); 2023 Scenario 1 requests USD 7.5M, Scenario 2 USD 5.2M; readiness costs 5% (S1)/6% (S2) of budget. Readiness+activation triggers can be reached same day if both met 4 days before landfall — CERF disburses 100% per pre-agreed proposals.

--- page 35 ---
Table: UNICEF sector-specific learning questions by sector — Cash (understand mechanisms enabling/hindering use of national social protection systems for AA, contribute to shock-responsive social protection policy dialogue); RCCE (best communication entry points for multi-sectoral messaging, two-way communication feedback mechanisms); Child Protection (AA entry points for family separation/VAC/GBV/SEA response, feasibility of cash-based CP interventions, MHPSS help-seeking); Nutrition (viable Nutrition-in-Emergencies interventions, NiE Minimum Service Package operational knowledge, AA principles for NiE planning); WASH (cash vs in-kind hygiene supply effectiveness, AA's role in hygiene/disease prevention, capacity-building needs e.g. provincial health offices water quality monitoring); Education (education items households spend on, communication materials' effect on education expenditures). Process learning section: Learning group covers documenting/understanding/sharing (process), monitoring delivery (data tracking), and post-activation qualitative/quantitative impact evaluation.

--- page 36 ---
Narrative: Process learning key themes numbered 1-6 (forecasting model/triggers suitability; coordination & partnerships/localization; AA intervention selection/design; AA financing/risk; implementation issues by cash modality; approach to learning/reporting/communication). Independent impact evaluation: OCHA to commission independent evaluation focused on delivery model (cash) and household income impact, overseen by ad-hoc learning/M&E committee chaired by OCHA, using UNEG/OECD-DAC criteria (relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability). Advocacy and public communication: RC/HC-requested "One UN" communications plan targeting humanitarian donors, GoP, stakeholders; principles include "One UN/One HCT" messaging and focus on affected people's stories.

Table continuation: UNFPA rows — (A) Multi-purpose cash for Health for Pregnant/vulnerable Women (1,350 HHs/8,370 individuals via ACCORD/PSRP/PLAN/LGUs); (B) SRH and protection commodities to pregnant/vulnerable women and girls; (C) Support relocation of at-risk health/birthing facilities (1,050 HHs/4,920 individuals via MOSEP/Plan International/LGUs) — activities include SRH/GBV sub-cluster activation, warehouse/logistics alerting, barangay health worker re-orientation, GBV/MHPSS referral pathway dissemination, SRH/GBV Surge team establishment, dignity kit/commodity distribution.

--- page 41 ---
Annex 2 - DRAFT trigger messages: Readiness trigger message (email template from RC/HC Gustavo Gonzalez to CERF secretariat) — states TC potential category ≥3 (>178km/h 1-min or 158km/h 10-min sustained wind) projected to impact Region 5/8 (or 8/13), Scenario 1 activated for readiness, funding requirement USD 7.5M (FAO/IOM/UNFPA/UNICEF/WFP); bracketed alt text for Scenario 2 USD 5.1M. Activation trigger message template — states activation threshold reached when predicted destroyed houses [XXX] at [xx%] probability falls within 50%@80,000 to 95%@5,000 range; activates CERF AA Framework within 72 hours (3 days) before projected landfall.

--- page 42 ---
Annex 3 - Evaluation of forecasts for anticipatory actions (April 2021): narrative on OCHA/HDX/AA Core Team model selection process among WFP, IFRC/DREF, Global Parametrics — recommendation to use IFRC/DREF model (operational track record, open source/free, full-country admin-3 coverage, developers open to adding PAGASA data). Table: "Evaluation Matrix" comparing IFRC/DREF vs Global Parametrics vs WFP across criteria — trigger based on public forecast data (Yes/Yes/Yes but WFP uses non-public PAGASA), PAGASA data use (No[510 exploring]/Yes/Yes), trigger simplicity (Partial ML model/Partial vulnerability-combined/Yes simple rainfall-anomaly threshold), impact-basis appropriateness (Yes % houses destroyed/Yes % houses destroyed/Yes people affected).

--- page 43 ---
Table continuation (Evaluation Matrix): lead time adequacy (Yes 72h+/Yes 72h+/N/A no forecasted hazard data), adaptability to OCHA specs by June (Yes/Partial needs budget/Likely not), editable output data (Yes/Yes/Probably), open source (Yes/No could be/No could be), cost to operationalize (Low/Medium/Unclear), cost to maintain (Low/Low-medium/Unclear), model performance (Precision/recall ~70%/accurately called major storms since 2019/Precision 17% for Bicol). "IFRC/DREF model card" begins: main contacts Aklilu Teklesadik & Marc van den Homberg (Netherlands Red Cross); output = map of predicted % completely damaged buildings per municipality, full Philippines at admin-3 resolution; hazard data = ECMWF TC/wind speed forecasts, vulnerability = NDRRMC housing damage reports.

--- page 44 ---
Narrative continuation (IFRC/DREF model card): methodology — Willoughby methodology for typhoon track wind fields, XGBoost correlating wind speed with damage by building material; trigger threshold = 10% houses totally damaged (per DROMIC) in ≥3 municipalities (1-in-5-year event); classification+regression models combined. Model evaluation: Precision/Recall/F1 ~0.7; regression MAE 3%, RMSE 7%; performance worsens with longer lead time. Operational readiness: continuously updated, used since 2019 (Tisoy 2019 small-scale, Ulysses 2020) but missed Goni (2020). Figure: "510 TYPHOON TRIGGER MODEL: Technical Overview" — schematic showing historical typhoons (Haiyan, Melor, Hagupit, Nammasun) training set with exposure/vulnerability indicators (roof type, poverty, wall type) + hazard indicators (rainfall, wind speed, typhoon path, sustained duration) → model relating to impact indicator (# damaged houses by municipality); prediction set (current typhoon e.g. Haima) combines new forecast data with pre-disaster indicators to predict % damaged houses via map output.

--- page 45 ---
"Global Parametrics model card" — contacts Toby Behrmann & Wendy Smith; output = probability of exceeding a specific wind speed at a location; geographic scope Salcedo, Eastern Samar (being expanded). Model development: hazard data from NASA/UKMET/NOAA/CPHC/JTWC/HPC/OPC/RSMC Nadi/TCWC Wellington/METEO France/TCWC Darwin/JMC/ECMWF/PAGASA; vulnerability = Oxfam socioeconomic/damage data (house construction); methodology computes typhoon track wind fields per ensemble member, fraction of ≥5 tracks above threshold at each exposure location; trigger = wind speed + probability components tuned via internal vulnerability assessment. Model evaluation: validated historically/real-time since 2019; performance depends mainly on input typhoon model error, not lead time. Operational readiness: constantly running/updated by Global Parametrics (Alin Radu, Thom Johnson); ready to deploy pending new geography additions; tested by Oxfam against 2019-2020 TCs (3 key events captured), further validation planned for 2021.

--- page 46 ---
Figure: Global Parametrics "Methodology" slide — TC Phanfone (22-12-19) example showing wind speed color scale (5-50 m/s), ensemble track map (pink lines = ensemble members, green/black = actual/mean track) over Philippines, and a risk/impact heatmap (blue-purple gradient) zoomed into a green-highlighted municipality (Salcedo, Eastern Samar). "WFP model card" begins: contact Analuisa Candenedo; output = anomalous rainfall % + impact trigger threshold; geographic scope = full national coverage, admin level 2 analysis; hazard data = NOAA IBTrACS storm track frequency + CHIRPS/PAGASA precipitation anomalies; vulnerability = ReliefWeb people-impacted data; methodology = binary classification of affected/not-affected combined with vulnerability/socioeconomic index into a risk index.

--- page 47 ---
Narrative continuation (WFP model card): trigger threshold defined via ROC curve on precipitation anomaly. Model evaluation: for Region V (Bicol), ROC curve gives 17% precision at optimal 28% rainfall anomaly threshold; performance not lead-time dependent (N/A, uses real-time not forecast data). Operational readiness: update/recalibration responsibility not specified; not yet used for AA (needs to switch from real-time to forecast data, possibly rainfall→wind speed) — used so far only to create a transparent trigger mechanism for response, not anticipatory action. Chart: "HAZARD TIMELINE – Region V" — dual-panel time series 2010-2021: top panel rainfall anomalies (%) fluctuating -50 to +150% with ~28% threshold line; bottom panel log-scale "Affected People" scatter by hazard type (Flood=blue, Tropical storms/typhoons=red, Dry spell=orange) ranging ~10^3 to 10^7 people, vertical lines linking anomaly spikes to affected-people events.
